pr.title: Name the Projector version in a review's header
pr.head: 1915627f3c84322560ebf41d37a86ecf8c4a2743

summary: Projector's review commands label every review they post, so a reader can tell a Projector review from a person's comment and weigh it by what produced it. While a review runs, project review setup posts a start comment on the pull request. When the review lands, project review publish opens its body with a visible signature line and a hidden HTML marker comment. All three name the model, and the reasoning effort when the host reports one.

None of them named the Projector release. The review method changes from release to release, so a reader comparing two reviews of one pull request could not tell which version of the method wrote each. This pull request adds a projector segment ahead of the model in the start comment and the signature line, and a matching projector= field in the marker:

📽️ **Projector review** · projector `0.6.9` · model `claude-opus-5-5` · effort `xhigh` · **CLEAN** · took 12m 34s

<!-- projector-review v=1 verdict=clean projector=0.6.9 model=claude-opus-5-5 effort=xhigh sha=… findings=0 seconds=754 covered=3/3 -->

The version comes from the installed projector-cli package, read the same way project --version reads it. A command run from a source checkout that was never installed writes unknown. To share that lookup with the review code, distribution_version moves from cli.py to core.py, because cli.py imports review.py and review.py cannot import cli.py back.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Start comment: the comment project review setup posts while a review runs, and publish deletes when the review lands.
  • Signature line: the first line of a published review's body, naming what produced it, the verdict, and how long it took.
  • Marker: the hidden <!-- projector-review … --> comment under the signature line, carrying the same facts as fields a program can read.
  • Distribution: the installed Python package, projector-cli, whose recorded version importlib.metadata reads.

cards.title: What the review found
cards.html:
The Projector review of this head is clean: no finding threads, and the repository's validation gate passed at 1915627. It left one suggestion, shown as a note on skills/review-pr/SKILL.md: the label names the CLI's release, and the method text comes from the plugin, which updates separately.

This head is the same commit that was reviewed clean on #176, which closed when the branch was reopened as this pull request.

groups.title: The header names the release
groups.kicker: How the start comment, signature line, and marker gain the projector segment
intro: Two functions in review.py write a review's labels. start_comment writes the start comment, and compose writes the published review's signature line and marker. Both now build their shared middle part with one helper, producer_segments, which returns the projector, model, and optional effort segments in that order.

compose then checks its own output against two regular expressions, SIGNATURE and MARKER, which describe the format review-pr/SKILL.md documents. Both now require the new segment and field. They check only the line compose has just written, so a review posted before this change is never tested against them.

checks.text: Reviews posted before this change still count in the collision check, the check that stops one account from posting two verdicts on one commit. The only code that reads an earlier review's marker is reviewer_verdicts, whose projector-review .* sha=<sha> filter matches a marker with or without projector=. Traced by reading every reader of the marker, and test_an_older_verdict_whose_marker_carries_effort_still_collides, which posts an old-format marker, passes at this head.

files.note: Adds producer_segments, uses it in start_comment and compose, and adds the segment and field to SIGNATURE and MARKER.

checks.text: producer_segments takes the version and effort as arguments rather than reading them itself, so compose reads each once and the signature line and marker cannot disagree.

Every start comment names the version. Both setup and move build the comment with start_comment, and the re-read after move edits the comment checks only sha=, so the longer text cannot fail it. Traced through both callers.

The marker requires projector= right after verdict=, so this check refuses a marker that leaves the version out. distribution_version always returns a value, unknown at worst, so compose never writes such a marker.

files.note: Pins the installed version to 1.2.3 for every review test, updates the exact-text assertions, and adds a test for the unknown case.

checks.text: The patch replaces importlib.metadata.version itself, which core.distribution_version looks up on each call, so the tests see one version whatever this machine has installed.
The full suite ran at this head: 429 tests, all passing, with one skip, the TypeScript build check that needs npm ci.

groups.title: One version lookup for the CLI and reviews
groups.kicker: Why distribution_version moves from cli.py to core.py
intro: distribution_version returns the version of the installed projector-cli package, which project --version prints and install.sh status compares against the release. It lived in cli.py. The review code now needs it too, but cli.py already imports review.py, so review.py importing cli.py would be circular. The function moves to core.py, which both modules already import. It behaves the same there. Only its docstring and the name it calls importlib.metadata by change.

checks.text: core.py imports importlib.metadata by its full name, not as metadata, because several of its functions already use metadata as a local variable for a plan's frontmatter.
With the head installed into a fresh virtual environment, start_comment wrote projector `0.6.9`. Run from the source tree with PYTHONPATH=src and no install, it wrote projector `unknown`.

files.note: Drops its own copy and imports DISTRIBUTION and distribution_version from core.

checks.text: cli.py still needs importlib.metadata for install_record, and importing both names back keeps project --version, the warning about a newer release, and the test_projector.py tests that import distribution_version from projector.cli working. The installed head printed project 0.6.9 for --version, and those tests pass.

groups.title: The documented format
groups.kicker: The skill and the CLI reference show the new segment
intro: skills/review-pr/SKILL.md is the instruction an agent follows to review a pull request, and it shows the exact start comment, signature line, and marker that project review writes. docs/cli.md is the command reference. Both now show the projector segment and say where its value comes from.

files.note: Adds the segment to both quoted formats and a paragraph on where the version comes from.

checks.text: The label names the release of the project command. The method text a review follows comes from the Projector plugin, which updates separately, so the two can differ when an upgraded CLI runs beside an older cached plugin, or the reverse. project upgrade updates both. The review left a suggestion to say so here.

files.note: The project review section says the start comment and signature line name the version that project --version reports.
